## HueMux v0.0.2-alpha.20 — GPL-3.0, signed releases, and upgrades that work

> **You must uninstall the old build before installing this one.** Read the
> first section — this is a one-time break and it cannot be avoided.

### Uninstall alpha.19 first

Every release up to alpha.19 was **debug-signed**, because no signing key
existed. This one is signed properly. Android identifies an app by its signing
key and refuses to upgrade across a change of key, so the install will fail
with a confusing error unless the old copy is removed first.

Uninstall, then install. Every release after this one upgrades normally.

Key fingerprint, if you want to verify a download is genuinely ours:

```
43:44:0F:03:F8:DF:CF:E2:23:C9:20:8F:5A:98:14:E2:4C:69:1C:84:DD:41:4A:DF:F7:C6:C4:ED:8E:E9:D0:60
```

### Every release so far could never have updated itself

`versionCode` was hardcoded to `1`. Android refuses to install a build whose
version code is not higher than the one already there, so all nineteen alphas
were, technically, apps incapable of updating. It never showed up because every
install was a fresh sideload over a wipe.

It now comes from the commit count, so it goes up on its own and nobody has to
remember it. `versionName` comes from the tag, which means the version shown in
the app is finally the version you installed rather than "0.0.1-alpha".

### Install and stay updated with Obtainium

[Obtainium](https://github.com/ImranR98/Obtainium) tracks GitHub releases
directly, so updates arrive without any app store:

1. Install Obtainium.
2. **Add App**, paste `https://github.com/zamber/huemux`.
3. Enable **Include prereleases** to follow alphas.

### The project has a licence now: GPL-3.0-or-later

The README used to say "Code: MIT", but no `LICENSE` file was ever committed —
so in law nothing had been granted, and nobody could legally redistribute or
package it. That is fixed, and the licence is **GPL-3.0-or-later**.

Practically: use it, change it, share it, but a version you hand out comes with
its source under the same terms. It also unblocks F-Droid, Flathub and
Homebrew, which all refuse unlicensed projects — see
[PUBLISHING.md](../../PUBLISHING.md) for what comes next there.

### No functional changes

Everything above is packaging and licensing. The app behaves exactly as
alpha.19 did.
